units.oneLiner: Keep every key in the slot array itself and, when the home slot is taken, probe the next slot and the next: the probes stay inside the cache line the first one fetched, Knuth's 1963 formulas say exactly what each load factor costs, and the price is clustering, which is why the table resizes before it is full and why the hash must scatter neighbors.
units.description: Open addressing with linear probing on a 65,536-slot table against Knuth's 1963 formulas (hits and misses within 1% at loads 0.25 to 0.7, within 8% at 0.9) and a Python set shadowing 1,200,000 mixed operations across six structures: at load 0.9 a hit costs 5.315 probes but 1.540 cache lines against 2.570 and 2.570 for double hashing and 2.450 and 2.450 for chaining; clusters of 715 slots and a probe variance of 277 where Robin Hood hashing keeps the same mean with variance 19.8; a miss at 5.864 probes under tombstones against 1.698 under backward-shift deletion after deleting half the keys; and a weak hash on consecutive keys costing 1,056 probes per hit against 8.3 for double hashing.
units.time: O(1) expected; (1 + 1/(1 - a)) / 2 probes per hit

units.plan_row: Open addressing × Linear probing. Puzzle 172, data-structures (problemSlug hash-collision-resolution, the atlas problem page carrying "Cache-friendly hashing"; sibling live lesson cuckoo-hashing-two-table-eviction-kicks). Solution open_addressing_linear_probing.py (3.0s, prints OK): linear probing with tombstone or backward-shift deletion and a rebuild at 85% live-plus-tombstones, quadratic probing (triangular offsets), double hashing (odd stride), separate chaining, Robin Hood, Fibonacci and weak hashes, a probe-and-cache-line counter (8 slots per 64-byte line, one line per chaining node). ORACLES: (1) Knuth 1963 at loads 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.7 / 0.8 / 0.9 / 0.95: hits 1.164 / 1.509 / 2.172 / 3.027 / 5.962 / 11.609 against 1.167 / 1.500 / 2.167 / 3.000 / 5.500 / 10.500, misses 1.397 / 2.510 / 5.971 / 12.655 / 50.434 / 205.639 against 1.389 / 2.500 / 6.056 / 13.000 / 50.500 / 200.500 (within 6% to 0.8, 20% beyond); (2) 1,200,000 mixed operations across six structures all matching a Python set, final sizes matching; (3) the race at load 0.9 (every key looked up, 5,000 misses): linear probing 5.315 probes/hit, 47.975/miss, 1.540 lines/hit, variance 277, max 612, longest cluster 715; Robin Hood 5.315 / 5.644 / 1.540 / 19.8 / 29; quadratic 2.850 / 12.055 / 1.951 / 16.2 / 92; double hashing 2.570 / 10.056 / 2.570 / 11.1 / 68; chaining 2.450 / 1.923 / 2.450 / 0.5 / 9; longest run by load 8 / 31 / 85 / 209 / 752 / 3,250; (4) deletion: fill to 0.7, delete half: tombstones 5.864 probes per miss (formula for 0.7: 6.056), backward shift 1.698 (formula for 0.35: 1.683); (5) weak hash (high bits) on 2,048 consecutive keys in 4,096 slots: linear probing 1,056 probes per hit, double hashing 8.3, chaining 402.8, strong hash 1.50. Honest: linear probing pays twice double hashing's probes at 0.9 and wins only on lines; the Robin Hood mean is identical to 1e-9 (the displacement total is invariant), asserted; three author notes recorded (quadratic vs double ordering; the first weak-hash experiment at 65,536 slots ran quadratic for ten minutes and was shrunk; a 5,000-key hit sample was replaced by every key after the early-inserted keys biased it). Cards: self, Hash table with chaining, Robin Hood hashing, Cuckoo hashing (live lesson badge) (all algoName). neverUse: linear probing with a hash that keeps neighbors neighbors. Figure: Knuth's hit and miss curves with the measured points beside bars of the longest run by load; cite Knuth 1963 / TAOCP 3 6.4, Amdahl et al. 1954, Pagh-Pagh-Ruzic STOC 2007 DOI 10.1145/1250790.1250839. Viz LinearProbingViz: a 64-slot table as eight cache lines filling to load 0.9, walked slots amber and touched lines outlined, the running average probes per insert against Knuth's expectation, every key checked reachable from its home each tick; NODE-VERIFIED 20 cycles x 21 ticks, 0 breaks; stepMs 500, holdTicks rests. Preserved narration: Aoede + Algieba.

units.oneLiner: Blur, take the gradient, keep only the local maxima along the gradient so every edge is one pixel thin, then decide with two thresholds instead of one: a pixel above the high threshold is an edge, and a pixel above the low threshold is an edge only if it connects through other candidates to a strong one, so faint stretches of real contours survive and isolated noise does not.
units.description: The Canny edge detector with hysteresis thresholding on a 96 x 96 image whose edges are known by construction (a disk 120 levels above the background and a square ramping from 30 to 120 above it): F1 1.000 noiseless and 1.000, 1.000, 0.980, 0.937 under noise of 8, 16, 24, 40 with 2 components every time; a single high threshold alone holds recall 0.82 at every level (the faint edges lost), the low threshold alone admits 751 pixels for 248 true at noise 40 (precision 0.33, 131 fragments), thresholded Sobel magnitude is 99% thick, Marr-Hildreth zero crossings reach recall 0.65 to 0.76 in 5 to 28 fragments; and the hysteresis invariant held pixel by pixel, 193 strong pixels pulling 48 weak ones through.
units.time: O(pixels) for blur, gradient, thinning, and one breadth-first search
units.space: a magnitude and a direction per pixel
units.baseline: Sobel magnitude with a single threshold

units.plan_row: Canny edge detector × Hysteresis thresholding. Puzzle 173, signal-graphics (problemSlug edge-detection, the atlas problem page carrying "Edge detection"). Solution canny_edge_detector_hysteresis_thresholding.py (0.4s, prints OK): a synthetic 96 x 96 image with ground-truth boundary pixels (disk at +120, square ramping +30 to +120), separable Gaussian blur (sigma 1.4), Sobel, non-maximum suppression with image-coordinate diagonals and one strict comparison, breadth-first hysteresis (high = half the peak gradient, low = 0.4 high), single-threshold ablations on thinned and raw magnitude, Marr-Hildreth LoG zero crossings with a slope test, a scorer (precision / recall / F1 within one pixel, thick = inside a filled 2 x 2 block, connected components), and a pixel-by-pixel hysteresis-invariant checker. ORACLES: (1) noiseless: precision 1.000, recall 1.000, 240 edge pixels for 248 true, thick 0.000, components 2; (2) the invariant at noise 8 / 16 / 24 / 40: 193 + 48, 193 + 48, 195 + 44, 194 + 47 strong + weak, every weak pixel connected to a strong one; (3) F1 by noise 8 / 16 / 24 / 40: Canny 1.000 / 1.000 / 0.980 / 0.937 (components 2 / 2 / 2 / 2); NMS + high only 0.900 / 0.898 / 0.898 / 0.895 (recall 0.82 / 0.82 / 0.82 / 0.81); NMS + low only 1.000 / 0.992 / 0.885 / 0.495 (precision at 40: 0.330, 751 pixels, 131 components); Sobel magnitude thresholded 0.831 / 0.848 / 0.854 / 0.855 (thick 1.000 / 0.987 / 0.987 / 0.994); Marr-Hildreth 0.865 / 0.833 / 0.785 / 0.789 (recall 0.76 / 0.71 / 0.65 / 0.72; 6 / 5 / 9 / 28 components). Honest: at noise 40 Canny's precision falls to 0.946 as speckles attach to true contours; three author corrections recorded (the first NMS mapped diagonals wrongly and kept tied pairs, 35% thick and 24 fragments noiseless; the thickness metric changed from three-or-more neighbors to a filled 2 x 2 block; the first image had constant-contrast edges so hysteresis had nothing to rescue, hence the ramped square). Cards: self, Sobel operator, Marr-Hildreth, Otsu thresholding (live lesson badge) (all algoName). neverUse: a single threshold on an image with faint and strong edges together. Figure: a schematic gradient profile along the ramped edge with both thresholds and noise spikes, beside F1 by noise for four methods; cite Canny TPAMI 1986 DOI 10.1109/TPAMI.1986.4767851, Marr and Hildreth 1980. Viz CannyViz: a 48 x 48 image (noise 16 / 28 / 40 by cycle) blurred, differentiated, and thinned at scene start, then hysteresis one breadth-first wave per tick, strong blue, rescued weak amber, unanchored gray, the connectivity invariant checked every tick; NODE-VERIFIED 12 cycles, 0 breaks; stepMs 450, holdTicks rests. Preserved narration: Aoede + Algieba.
